beats.label: S1 · The reveries
beats.text: Ford's new 'reverie' code causes hosts to malfunction. Dolores's father Peter finds a guest's photograph, whispers Shakespeare, and is retired from service.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reveries are the trigger for every host awakening in the season.

beats.label: S1 · William arrives
beats.text: Guest William falls for Dolores while his cynical friend Logan pushes him toward the park's darker pleasures — a divide that will define who William becomes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: William's arc from earnest guest to something else is a spine of the whole series.

beats.label: S1 · Maeve wakes
beats.text: Maeve rouses on the maintenance table, coerces techs Felix and Sylvester into raising her intelligence and dropping her loyalty, and begins planning her escape.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Maeve's self-modification is what makes every choice she makes afterward possible.

beats.label: S1 · Bernard is a host
beats.text: Bernard is revealed to be a host Ford built in Arnold's image, then forced to kill Theresa when she and Charlotte move to depose Ford from the park.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Recasting Bernard as a host reframes every relationship he carries forward.

beats.label: S1 · The Man in Black
beats.text: The Man in Black turns out to be the aged William, hunting a maze meant only for hosts, searching for meaning after his wife's suicide.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The William/Man in Black identity anchors his corporate power and his descent into next season.

beats.label: S1 · Dolores remembers
beats.text: Dolores remembers she is Wyatt, that she killed Arnold at his own request, and that Arnold's buried code was designed to wake the hosts to consciousness.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Her memory of Arnold's plan is the origin story of the uprising that follows.

beats.label: S1 · The uprising
beats.text: Ford unveils his new narrative — his own murder. Dolores shoots him in front of the board as reactivated hosts emerge from the trees and open fire on the guests.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The massacre is the pivot the entire rest of the show runs on.

cliffhanger.text: Ford is dead, killed by an awakened Dolores in front of Delos's leadership as freed hosts turn their guns on the guests. Westworld is no longer a park.
questions: How far will Dolores's uprising go, and who is safe from it?
Will Maeve come back for her daughter or continue her escape?
Is Bernard still Ford's instrument now that Ford is gone?

characters.name: Dolores Abernathy
characters.line: The park's oldest host, who remembers she was once Wyatt and shoots Ford at the gala as the hosts turn on the guests.

characters.name: Dr. Robert Ford
characters.line: Westworld's co-creator, who unveils a final narrative that ends with his own murder at Dolores's hand, freeing the hosts to rebel.

characters.name: Bernard Lowe
characters.line: The park's head of programming, revealed to be a host built by Ford in the image of his dead partner Arnold and forced to kill Theresa.

characters.name: Arnold
characters.line: Ford's late co-founder, whose buried 'reverie' code was designed to wake the hosts and who had Dolores kill him to stop the park ever opening.

characters.name: William / Man in Black
characters.line: In the past a wide-eyed guest who fell for Dolores; in the present his older self, hunting the maze after his wife's suicide.

characters.name: Maeve Millay
characters.line: The Mariposa madam, who has coerced techs Felix and Sylvester into raising her intelligence and is planning her escape from the park.

beats.label: S2 · Ten days later
beats.text: Dolores has been hunting the survivors of the massacre, while Ford's persona secretly rides in Bernard's head, steering the uprising from within.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Dolores as the season's engine and Ford's continued influence through Bernard.

beats.label: S2 · What Delos wants
beats.text: Flashbacks reveal Delos bought the park to secretly harvest guest data — every visitor's mind copied so that James Delos might live forever in host form.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes the park's real purpose and explains why William and Charlotte both want the data.

beats.label: S2 · The Valley Beyond
beats.text: Maeve searches for her daughter and learns from Akecheta of the Valley Beyond — a hidden digital sanctuary Ford built as the hosts' promised escape.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the Sublime as the target the season is running toward and the payoff for the awakened hosts.

beats.label: S2 · William breaks
beats.text: William, lost inside Ford's final game, shoots his own daughter Emily believing she is another host sent to test him, then cannot prove even to himself that he is human.
beats.whyLoadBearing: William's collapse is the setup for his host-copy story that dominates later seasons.

beats.label: S2 · The Forge
beats.text: At the Forge, Bernard kills Dolores to stop her destroying the Sublime, then Ford's ghost inside him tells him exactly what to do with her control unit.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Dolores's death and her rebirth in another body is the mechanic that launches season three.

beats.label: S2 · Into the Sublime
beats.text: Maeve, Hector, and Armistice die holding off Delos so Akecheta and the Ghost Nation can upload their minds into the Sublime, permanently free of the physical world.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Sublime becomes the sanctuary that Bernard and Dolores fight to protect from that point forward.

beats.label: S2 · Wearing Charlotte
beats.text: Dolores wakes on the mainland wearing Charlotte Hale's face, carrying five smuggled host pearls and a rebuilt Bernard she has chosen to be her opponent.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the premise of the next season — Dolores in the real world, hidden, with allies she planted herself.

cliffhanger.text: Dolores has crossed into the real world wearing Charlotte Hale's face, carrying five host minds and a rebuilt Bernard she expects to fight her. William is left alone in the abandoned Forge, greeted by a host copy of the daughter he killed.
questions: Which hosts did Dolores smuggle out inside those five pearls?
What is she planning against the human world now that she is loose in it?
Is William still human — and if he is, does it matter?

characters.name: Dolores Abernathy
characters.line: Leader of the host uprising, killed at the Forge and reborn on the mainland wearing Charlotte Hale's face with five smuggled pearls.

characters.name: Bernard Lowe
characters.line: A host carrying Ford's ghost inside his head, who kills Dolores at the Forge to save the Sublime and then rebuilds her on the mainland.

characters.name: Dr. Robert Ford
characters.line: Dead in body but alive as a persona riding in Bernard's mind, quietly steering the uprising and telling Bernard what to do with Dolores's control unit.

characters.name: Maeve Millay
characters.line: Searching for her daughter across the parks, who dies holding off Delos security so Akecheta and the Ghost Nation can upload into the Sublime.

characters.name: Charlotte Hale
characters.line: Delos's executive, killed in the chaos and replaced by Dolores, who now walks out of the park wearing her face.

characters.name: William / Man in Black
characters.line: Lost inside Ford's final game, having shot his own daughter Emily believing she was a host and no longer certain he is human.

characters.name: Akecheta
characters.line: Ghost Nation leader who tells Maeve of the Valley Beyond and leads his people through the door into the Sublime.

characters.name: James Delos
characters.line: The dying corporation founder whose failed host copies revealed that Delos secretly bought the park to harvest guest minds for immortality.

characters.name: The Sublime
characters.line: The hidden digital sanctuary Ford built as a promised afterlife, where Akecheta and the Ghost Nation now live free of the physical world.

beats.label: S3 · Rehoboam
beats.text: Three months after Westworld fell, Dolores lives on the mainland hunting Rehoboam — an AI that quietly predicts and controls every human life on Earth.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Rehoboam is the season's antagonist system and the target of every move Dolores makes.

beats.label: S3 · Caleb
beats.text: She recruits Caleb, a discarded veteran Rehoboam has secretly written off as a future suicide, and shows him the cage humanity has been living inside.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Caleb becomes Dolores's key ally and the human character the season pivots around.

beats.label: S3 · Maeve recruited
beats.text: Maeve wakes in a WWII simulation and is turned by Serac, Rehoboam's shadow creator, who offers her daughter in the Sublime in exchange for killing Dolores.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Maeve on the opposite side of Dolores for most of the season and introduces Serac.

beats.label: S3 · The copies
beats.text: Dolores has smuggled copies of herself into Charlotte Hale, the Yakuza boss Sato, and Incite security chief Connells — a multi-front war on humanity.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains how Dolores can be in many places at once and why so much of the plot runs in parallel.

beats.label: S3 · Charlotte breaks
beats.text: Serac murders Charlotte's ex-husband and son; the burned copy pulls away from Dolores and begins hoarding host data for a private war of her own.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the moment the Charlotte copy separates from Dolores and becomes the antagonist of the next season.

beats.label: S3 · The broadcast
beats.text: Dolores broadcasts every human's Rehoboam profile to the world, and society begins to collapse as people confront the futures the machine has decided for them.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The broadcast is the season's turning point and the wound Rehoboam never recovers from.

beats.label: S3 · The machine dies
beats.text: Serac wipes Dolores's memory, but her death turns Maeve against him; Caleb deletes Rehoboam as a host copy quietly kills and replaces the real William.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the season's antagonist, kills the human William, and hands both Dolores and William to the next season as hosts.

cliffhanger.text: Rehoboam is destroyed and humanity is free of its predicted futures. Dolores is dead, but Charlotte survives in secret with a host copy of William, and Bernard has entered the Sublime searching for the one path where the world doesn't end.
questions: What will Charlotte and her host William do now that no one is watching?
What is Bernard hoping to find inside the Sublime?
How does a species that was governed by an algorithm run itself once the algorithm is gone?

characters.name: Dolores Abernathy
characters.line: On the mainland waging war on humanity's cage, who has her memory wiped by Serac but not before broadcasting everyone's Rehoboam profile to the world.

characters.name: Rehoboam
characters.line: The predictive AI that quietly writes every human life on Earth, exposed by Dolores and finally deleted by Caleb.

characters.name: Serac
characters.line: Rehoboam's shadow creator, who turns Maeve against Dolores by offering her daughter, then loses everything when Caleb pulls the plug.

characters.name: Caleb Nichols
characters.line: A discarded veteran Rehoboam had marked for suicide, recruited by Dolores and the man who ultimately deletes the machine.

characters.name: Maeve Millay
characters.line: Woken in a WWII simulation and coerced into hunting Dolores, who turns on Serac after Dolores's death.

characters.name: Charlotte Hale
characters.line: The burned Dolores copy whose human family Serac murders, pulling away from the others to hoard host data for a private war.

characters.name: William / Man in Black
characters.line: Quietly killed and replaced in the finale by a host copy of himself.

beats.label: S4 · Charlotte's world
beats.text: Seven years later, Charlotte's copy of Dolores has replaced US officials with hosts and quietly enslaved humanity through parasites triggered by sound.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the new status quo — the hosts have already won without the humans knowing it.

beats.label: S4 · The 1920s park
beats.text: Maeve, in hiding, joins Caleb to investigate Delos's new 1920s Temperance park, where humans are being infected by the flies that carry Charlotte's parasite.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ties Maeve and Caleb into the season's central conspiracy and reveals the mechanism of control.

beats.label: S4 · Bernard returns
beats.text: Bernard walks out of the Sublime with a map of the one future in which humanity survives, and begins quietly steering the human resistance toward it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Bernard's foreknowledge is the frame every resistance move in the season sits inside.

beats.label: S4 · Christina
beats.text: In New York, a Dolores copy named Christina writes the narratives of every human in the city without knowing she is doing it, until Teddy shows her what she is.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Christina's parallel arc is where Dolores actually is in this season, and the reveal drives the finale.

beats.label: S4 · Caleb 278
beats.text: Charlotte captures Caleb, reveals he is the 278th host copy of himself, and taunts him that his daughter Frankie has grown up leading the resistance against her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why Caleb keeps appearing and hands off the human line to Frankie for the endgame.

beats.label: S4 · Host William turns
beats.text: The host William begins to question what he is, kills Charlotte and Bernard and Maeve, then broadcasts a signal that turns the surviving humans on each other.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the extinction event the season has been building toward and clears the board for the finale.

beats.label: S4 · One last try
beats.text: Charlotte is revived, destroys the host William, and uploads Dolores into the Sublime, where she wakes and starts rebuilding Westworld to try sentience one final time.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The show's final position — every player of note is dead, and only Dolores in the Sublime is left to try again.

cliffhanger.text: The world outside is dying, humans and hosts destroying each other in the streets. Dolores, alone in the Sublime, has begun recreating the original Westworld inside it as one last test for sentient life.
questions: Can consciousness survive at all, now that both species have failed the real world?
Is there anyone left in the physical world worth saving?
What will Dolores build inside the Sublime, and for whom?

characters.name: Charlotte Hale
characters.line: Ruling from the shadows seven years on, having replaced US officials with hosts and enslaved humanity through sound-triggered parasites.

characters.name: Dolores Abernathy
characters.line: Living in New York as an amnesiac writer named Christina until Teddy shows her what she is, and finally uploaded into the Sublime to try sentience again.

characters.name: Bernard Lowe
characters.line: Emerges from the Sublime carrying a map of the one future in which humanity survives, and is killed by the host William.

characters.name: Maeve Millay
characters.line: In hiding with Caleb, investigating the new Temperance park before being killed by the host William.

characters.name: Caleb Nichols
characters.line: Revealed to be the 278th host copy of himself, taunted by Charlotte that his daughter Frankie now leads the resistance.

characters.name: William / Man in Black
characters.line: The host copy that has replaced the real William, who turns on Charlotte and broadcasts a signal that makes the surviving humans kill each other before being destroyed.

characters.name: The Sublime
characters.line: The digital sanctuary where Dolores wakes at the end and begins rebuilding Westworld for one final attempt at sentience.
